body.statement: Consider the one-dimensional iid Gaussian subexperiment with \(r=2,J=3,K=L=2\), \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \(T_1/n\to\lambda=1\), \(S=I_2\), and \(\rho=1/20\). Fix \(U_D=[(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)]\), \(\mu_0=(3/2,3/2)^{\prime}\), \(f_{\mathrm{post}}=(1,0)^{\prime}\), \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,4,1)\) in target--donor order, and independent Gaussian errors across every pre and post date. Let the scalar \(a>0\) multiply the first pre-factor row, so \(F_{\mathrm{pre}}(a)=\operatorname{diag}(a,1)\), and take the scalar chart \(\xi(\theta)=a-1\). The center \(a=1\) has \(F_{\mathrm{pre},0}=I_2\), \(A_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(a_{0,0}=(3/2,3/2)^{\prime}\), \(d_0=(0,1,0)^{\prime}\), \(c_{0,0}=d_0^{\prime}A_0^+a_{0,0}=3/2\), \(X_0=A_0\), and \(x_0=a_{0,0}\). The path \(a_n(u)=1+u/\sqrt n\) varies only this first pre-factor row; \(U_D,\mu_0,f_{\mathrm{post}},S,\rho,\Sigma,p,\lambda\), the Gaussian error law, and every other nuisance coordinate are fixed. Along this path \(d_n(u)^{\prime}A_n(u)^+a_{0,n}(u)=3/2\), so \(\dot c(u)=0\). Hence \(A_n(u)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1+u/\sqrt n&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(a_{0,n}(u)=(3(1+u/\sqrt n)/2,3/2)^{\prime}\), and \(d_n(u)=d_0\), so the post sample carries no information about \(u\). At the center, with \(v=(s,1-s)\), \(w_{P_{\theta_0}}(v)=(0,z,1-z)\), \(z=\operatorname{clip}((40s-9)/22,0,1)\), \(b_0=c_{0,0}-d_0^{\prime}w_0=1/2\) at \(s_0=31/40\), and \(R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v)=17/4-5z+6z^2\). Query \(v_n(t)=(s_0+t/\sqrt n,1-s_0-t/\sqrt n)\) for \(|t|\le L_0/\sqrt2\). The affected first-block mean derivative in target--donor order is \(D m_1=(3/2,0,1,0)^{\prime}\), while every other mean and covariance derivative is zero. Therefore the information per \(n\) observations is exactly \(I=p_1D m_1^{\prime}\Sigma^{-1}D m_1=\tfrac12\{9/4+1/4\}=5/4\). The upper KKT boundary has derivative \(-31/80\) in \(a\), while the unclipped second-donor weight has derivatives \(20/11\) in \(s\) and \(31/44\) in \(a\); since the centered risk derivative satisfies \(R_{P_{\theta_0}}^{\prime}(1)=7\), the local curve is \(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)=7\min\{(20/11)t+(31/44)u,0\}\). For \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and \(0<m=m_{\mathrm{half}}\le\min\{M,80L_0/(31\sqrt2)\}\), the query set contains a point at which both curves for \(u\in\{-m,m\}\) are unsaturated, and the exact binary minimax width is \((217m/22)\max\{\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-2m\sqrt{5/4})-\alpha,0\}\). The decision rule is on its unsaturated positive branch exactly when additionally \(m<z_{1-\alpha}/\sqrt{5/4}\); on that interval the maximum operator may be deleted.
body.justification: The explicit hinge verifies that the local graph is nonconstant at a moving boundary and that zero extra simultaneous-graph cost remains possible.
body.gap: No cited synthetic-control result solves this bounded Gaussian confidence decision; the calculation is a falsifiable sanity reduction, not the full multidimensional theorem.
body.consumer: The smallest nontrivial implementation test has a closed-form benchmark against which the certified program can be checked.
